prerequisites: Bachelor's degree in an engineering discipline

learning_outcomes.text: Students will have a profound knowledge of the innovation process in companies and the most important tools for market-oriented and user-centered development of innovative technical products.

Students will have the knowledge and skills to analyze, plan, organize, and control innovation processes, conduct strategic product planning, apply methods for finding innovative products, and integrate appropriate controlling to achieve goals.

Students will analyze potentials for innovative products in practice for given topics through the use of observation methods and surveys, considering gender and diversity aspects. They will formulate a corresponding development order for an identified problem and develop requirement lists based on this.
Students will be able to select and apply suitable methods for problem identification and idea generation, depending on the individual application case.
Students will be able to apply methods for problem identification and, using creativity methods, initiate innovation projects in companies.
Students will be able to defend and critically evaluate their projects interdisciplinarily, especially before representatives of various disciplines.
Students will be able to identify innovation needs and projects in the context of companies, markets, and the environment, and methodically develop designs for innovative products.

syllabus_topics: Analysis Methods as a Basis for New Product Policy
Finding Ideas for New Products and Product Programs
Decision for Future Market and Product Policy
Organization and Processes of Integrated Product Development
Problem-solving and Idea Generation Methods such as Contradiction Methods (TRIZ, WOIZ), Synectics, Bionics etc.
assessment_rules: The portfolio examination is evaluated with a point system, with a maximum of 100 points achievable. The examination consists of three presentations and an oral project report. Each of the first two presentations can earn a maximum of 20 points, the oral project report a maximum of 40 points, and the final product presentation and project report a maximum of 20 points.
